name: Trans Am
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: Three friends from suburban Maryland fired their singer, plugged in a Casio and named the band after a Pontiac. Thirty years on, they're still poking post-rock with vocoders and Van Halen.

eras.title: Three campuses, one band
eras.text: Nathan Means, Philip Manley and Sebastian Thomson grew up around North Bethesda, Maryland, and started Trans Am while at three different colleges. They came up in the shadow of Fugazi and Bad Brains, and never quite fit the D.C. scene.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trans Am (band) · Bandcamp Daily: How the Eagles Inspired Trans Am's Latest Anti-Post-Rock Record · The Skinny: Sebastian Thomson on 20 years of Trans Am
years.h: Three students at three colleges start a band
years.p: [[Nathan Means|69f424b6-d8d3-4618-b123-ee4cd109d3f2]] at UNC Chapel Hill, [[Philip Manley|726b1239-9ca1-4239-b0a0-2d64d0ec6683]] at Oberlin and [[Sebastian Thomson|8b52879b-4983-4ab0-97b7-5b5d955381b8]] at Bard rehearse when they can, then move to Maryland after graduating.
years.xp:
Manley later said living in the same place turned out to be much harder than the long-distance setup they started with.

The Skinny puts the formation in the mid-1990s in Washington, D.C.; Wikipedia and Thrill Jockey point to 1990 and North Bethesda. All three grew up around there.

years.big: "Fuck a Corvette. We should call it Trans Am."
years.src: Phoenix New Times: Two Decades Deep
years.h: Corvette loses to the Pontiac
years.p: Manley pitches Corvette as the band's name. [[Sebastian Thomson|8b52879b-4983-4ab0-97b7-5b5d955381b8]] shoots it down in favor of the Pontiac, and the car wins.
years.xp: The Pontiac won. Thomson told the story to Phoenix New Times in 2014, twenty-odd years into the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trans Am (band) · Phoenix New Times: Two Decades Deep
years.h: The singer stops showing up, so Trans Am stops having one
years.p: A friend on vocals keeps skipping rehearsal. The band fires him and never replaces him, and ends up instrumental by accident.
years.xp: "We did have a singer, a friend of ours, and he would never show up," Thomson told Phoenix New Times.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trans Am (band) · The Skinny: Sebastian Thomson on 20 years of Trans Am · Tokafi: Interview with Phil Manley
years.h: Then a Casio shows up
years.p: Around 1993, in North Carolina, the band plugs in a cheap keyboard and decides it can be a punk instrument. The D.C. records give way to Kraftwerk, Aphex Twin and Autechre.
years.xp:
Thomson says they were floundering until the Casio. The early touchstones had been [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] and [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]]; after it the list ran through Chrome, This Heat, Van Halen, Manowar, Kraftwerk, Aphex Twin and Autechre.

Manley has said Trans Am owes more to Kraftwerk and early electronica than to krautrock. The clip is from the band's second live show, at The Cave in Chapel Hill.

years.big: "The D.C. scene was very self-serious and very political."
years.src: Phoenix New Times: Two Decades Deep · The Skinny: Sebastian Thomson on 20 years of Trans Am
years.h: The D.C. histories skip Trans Am
years.p: Manley on why the band, from the Maryland suburbs, never felt part of the hardcore scene. [[Nathan Means|69f424b6-d8d3-4618-b123-ee4cd109d3f2]] says it has a bigger national profile than most D.C. bands and still gets left out.
years.xp: Thomson told The Skinny the band was always a little left out, partly because it wanted to have fun. Means told Phoenix New Times the same thing from the other side: a bigger profile than all but a few D.C. bands, and still missing from the story.

eras.title: Tortoise's opening act, with Moogs
eras.text: Thrill Jockey signed them, John McEntire produced them, and Tortoise took them on the road. Critics filed Trans Am under post-rock; the band kept adding synths and arena-rock guitar until it started singing through a vocoder.

years.h: Trans Am lands the same day as Tortoise's big record
years.p: The 30-minute debut, recorded at Idful in Chicago with [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]], comes out January 30 alongside Tortoise's Millions Now Living Will Never Die. The cover reuses art from a 1980 National Geographic flexi disc, Space Sounds.
years.xp: Guitar Player heard a musicianly spacerock meltdown full of Moog blasts; AllMusic's Sean Cooper found it enjoyable but somewhat expendable. Some guitar parts drew comparisons to Foreigner and Boston.

years.h: Tortoise takes Trans Am on the road
years.p: After McEntire produces the debut, Trans Am tours the US supporting his band [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]].

years.h: Starjammer ends up on a Gilles Deleuze tribute
years.p: The track first appears on a split single with [[Wingtip Sloat|949a298b-bd56-493d-ad2c-65aa54fc266e]] on Tuba Frenzy. The German label Mille Plateaux later puts it on In Memoriam Gilles Deleuze.

years.h: Surrender to the Night arrives a year to the day later
years.p: Trans Am's second album, again with McEntire, comes out January 30, 1997. Entertainment Weekly hears Wire-esque jaggedness, arena-rock machismo and dance beats.
years.xp: The Washington Post called it a band pushing all the dance, noise and punk envelopes. The longest track, Carboforce, runs almost eight minutes.

years.h: The Surveillance makes it three records in three years
years.p: The third Thrill Jockey album lands between Surrender to the Night and Futureworld.

years.h: Trans Am opens its mouth, through a vocoder
years.p: On Futureworld, the fourth album, the instrumental band adds lyrics for the first time, all run through vocoders. The Village Voice calls it the band's definitive futurist new wave statement.
years.xp: The band produced it themselves. Pitchfork gave it 8.0; Trouser Press thought the robot singing took a back seat to grooves that nearly imprison the songs.

eras.title: Jokes, and the critics who weren't sure
eras.text: With their own studio in D.C., Trans Am made a 73-minute double album, then a synth-pop record critics took as a joke and a political one aimed at the Bush White House. The band has said the jokes were never only jokes.

years.h: Red Line stretches the Windows 98 startup chime into a song
years.p: The 24-track, 73-minute double album, made at Trans Am's own National Recording Studio, slows the chime down into Let's Take the Fresh Step Together. [[Ian Svenonius|0ef9be87-0dbe-4551-a526-f3f6891a2e9d]] guests on Ragged Agenda.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 8.7. The New York Times said the band had finally embraced free-form rock with a beat, and Trouser Press called it a sprawling career summary of the band's obsessions.

years.h: The odds and ends get a record of their own
years.p: You Can Always Get What You Want gathers Trans Am's rarities and non-album tracks on Thrill Jockey.

years.big: "There's nothing in our music which is a joke to us."
years.src: Wikipedia: TA (album) · Wikipedia: Trans Am (band) · The Skinny: Sebastian Thomson on 20 years of Trans Am
years.h: Critics hear a joke in TA, and Pitchfork gives it 3.5
years.p: Thomson's answer to The Skinny. The sixth album, co-produced with McEntire, goes slick and synthetic; he calls it a reaction against post-rock's seriousness.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the record parodies REO Speedwagon's look and was mostly panned. Thomson told The Skinny in 2014 that critics often misread it.

years.h: Liberation aims at the Bush White House
years.p: The seventh album takes on George W. Bush's presidency, the 2003 invasion of Iraq, the war on terror and propaganda.

eras.title: Opening for Tool
eras.text: Trans Am took its analog synths into arenas in front of Tool fans, soundtracked a PlayStation Portable game and put out fifteen years of live tapes. The label it had been on since 1996 was turning fifteen too.

years.cap: Trans Am at The Mohawk, Austin, November 15, 2007
years.h: Sex Change comes out and the van heads out with Zombi
years.p: The eighth album arrives February 20, and a US tour with [[Zombi|aa3dbea9-a183-42d4-8b30-a894d1fa3844]] and [[The Psychic Paramount|5f9a7c33-f744-4749-beb1-4e8ed69edd37]] follows. Pitchfork gives it 7.0.

years.h: Seventeen nights opening for Tool
years.p: The Maryland trio warms up arena crowds for [[Tool|66fc5bf8-daa4-4241-b378-9bc9077939d2]], the biggest stages of its career.

years.h: Thrill Jockey turns 15 and Trans Am plays the party
years.p: The band plays the label's 15th anniversary show in Chicago, and scores the PSP game After Burner: Black Falcon.

years.h: Live Trans Am from 1993 to 2008, 1,500 copies
years.p: What Day Is It Tonight? spans fifteen years of shows. Thrill Jockey's upload of the 1993 Chapel Hill set comes from its DVD.

years.h: Thing makes it nine studio albums
years.p: Trans Am's ninth studio album, again on Thrill Jockey.

eras.title: Three cities, one consensus
eras.text: By the 2010s Thomson lived in Brooklyn, Manley in the Bay Area and Means in Portland, and Thomson had a second job drumming for Baroness. The band met up when it could and kept making records by consensus.

years.h: Thomson picks up a second band, Baroness
years.p: The Savannah metal band hires drummer Sebastian Thomson after its own drummer retires following the band's bus accident. He plays on Purple, Gold & Grey and Stone.

years.src: The Skinny: Sebastian Thomson on 20 years of Trans Am
years.h: Ten albums in, they still live in different cities
years.p: Thomson tells The Skinny the secret to lasting is simple: they still like each other, and they don't live in the same city.
years.xp: Thomson on the title: "It's volume ten, as in 'Turn it up to ten!'" By then he lived in Brooklyn, Manley in the Bay Area and Means in Portland.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily: How the Eagles Inspired Trans Am's Latest Anti-Post-Rock Record · Thrill Jockey: Trans Am
years.h: Election night, and the band keeps recording
years.p: Trans Am is in San Francisco making California Hotel when the 2016 result comes in. Thrill Jockey says the band worked that night into the album.
years.xp: Bandcamp Daily reports the song Staying Power was cut right after the result, and the band nailed it in one take.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily: How the Eagles Inspired Trans Am's Latest Anti-Post-Rock Record · Thrill Jockey: Trans Am
years.h: California Hotel is named for a hotel off I-580, and a late Eagle
years.p: Recorded live at El Studio in San Francisco over four one-week sessions in two years. The title comes from a hotel Philip Manley saw off I-580 in Oakland; Thrill Jockey says it also honors the late Glenn Frey.
years.xp:
Manley told Bandcamp Daily the hotel name was just stupid enough to be a Trans Am title. On the Eagles: "I completely understand why someone would hate The Eagles. I used to hate The Eagles."

Vintage Moog, Micro-Korg and Crumar synths are all over it.

years.h: Thomson sits in with Late Night with Seth Meyers
years.p: Trans Am's drummer spends a week, May 20 to 23, as guest drummer for the NBC show's band.
